facts.raw_span: A man in his late 60s presented for evaluation of a right iris lesion
Visual acuity was 20/25 OU
The eye was pseudophakic
10 × 9 × 3.5-mm, well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan, peripheral iris nodule between the 3- and 6-o'clock positions
episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement
no visible iris seeding or aqueous cells
Ultrasonographic biomicroscopy: Showed ciliary body involvement
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy results: Showed monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes
Few CD3+, reactive T lymphocytes were present
Systemic evaluation: Showed no other involvement
Staging: T2N0M0
Image A: Well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris lesion

concepts.why: The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule and the fine-needle aspiration biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes support the diagnosis of primary iris lymphoma.

The presence of a peripheral iris nodule and ciliary body involvement on ultrasonographic biomicroscopy could suggest iris metastasis, although the absence of systemic involvement makes this less likely.

The presence of episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement could suggest uveitic glaucoma, although the absence of visible iris seeding or aqueous cells makes this less likely.

The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule could suggest iris melanoma, although the fine-needle aspiration biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes make this less likely.
The presence of episcleral sentinel vessels and anterior chamber angle involvement could suggest chronic iritis, although the absence of visible iris seeding or aqueous cells makes this less likely.

The presence of a well-delineated, bilobed, vascularized, tan iris nodule could suggest an iris cyst, although the fine-needle aspiration biopsy results showing a monomorphic population of small to medium-sized hyperchromatic, CD20+ lymphocytes make this less likely.
The patient's age and the presence of a pseudophakic eye could suggest age-related macular degeneration, although the primary complaint is related to the iris lesion.
The presence of episcleral sentinel vessels could suggest posterior scleritis, although the absence of other symptoms such as pain or redness makes this less likely.
The staging of T2N0M0 explains the localized nature of the iris lesion.
